newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto turns fast-food restaurant critic.
newsitem.headline: Suharto turns fast-food restaurant critic.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto has warned that imported western-style fast food threaten the popularity of local fare and has called for a curb on fast-food franchises, the Jakarta Post newspaper said on Friday.
Food Minister Ibrahim Hasan quoted Suharto as saying that the presence of fast-food restaurants was posing a threat to the popularity of traditional foods.
"The president wanted us to find a solution, that is not against international free trade principles, to curb the foreign franchise business," Ibrahim said after meeting with Suharto.

Foreign food and beverage chains, which have recently become popular with the burgeoning middle class in Indonesia's big cities, are only allowed to operate under franchising agreements with local firms.
The number of franchises has grown rapidly over recent years, rising from six in 1991 to over 118 last year, the newspaper said.
Fast-food chains operating in Indonesia include McDonald's, Pepsico Inc's Pizza Hut and Kentucky Fried Chicken, Wendy's and Allied Domecq Retailing International's Dunkin' Donuts.
